chapters.title: Chapter 898: Your Worst Enemy
paragraphs: Broken had already arrived at Deadbay City, where the massive Ship Golem awaited him, docked and ready. The full crew of the Vensalor Outriders stood assembled as well, prepared for the long voyage ahead. SexyGrill and her guild members were already aboard, and Vallrick, stood with his arms crossed near the boarding ramp, waiting silently but with clear anticipation.

The ship began to pull away from the harbor slowly, its great limbs moving with a mechanical grace. The people of Deadbay City gathered along the docks, waving farewell as the towering ship began to drift into the open sea.
Broken, however, stayed out of sight.

He had deliberately kept his presence hidden. As much as the citizens respected and admired him, he couldn't afford to draw attention. Not when his movements could reveal too much. Too many eyes were watching. Too many ears were listening.

His ability to travel swiftly between the ship, Slumdon Town, and even the capital of Dissidia Kingdom was something he kept as one of his greatest secrets. It was a tactical edge. One that none of his enemies knew he possessed, and he intended to keep it that way.
Only after the ship had left the port, when the silhouettes of the city's towers were nothing but fading lines on the horizon, did Broken finally step onto the upper deck.
The wind was steady. The sky stretched wide and clear above them.
This was it, another long journey.
But this time, even longer. Even farther.
They would cross the open ocean, venture past the Central Continent's far edges, and press onward toward the mysterious and dangerous lands of the North Continent.
A place few had dared to explore.
This wouldn't be a simple voyage.
"We'll be passing along the western edge of the Central Continent," Mizuki began, standing confidently at the front of the control room.
She tapped the floating map of Yunatea, expanding it mid-air for everyone to see. A glowing line marked their proposed route—skirting far from the main coastlines, deep into neutral waters.

"We can't afford to bring the ship too close to the Central Continent's mainland," she continued, her tone serious. "The closer we sail, the easier it is for our enemies to detect us. And we all know, King Broken's movements are constantly being watched."
The room fell into a brief hush, heads nodding in agreement.
"When we reach the northern quadrant of the Central Continent's sea," she added, "Queen Nerisa's forces will rendezvous with us and escort us the rest of the way to the North Continent."
Her lips curled into a confident grin as she turned to Broken. "So, what do you think, King?"
Broken folded his arms and gave a slight nod. "Sounds simple when explained like that. But have any of you actually crossed that part of the ocean? Any other threats we should be ready for?"

Ronan, standing near one of the display panels, stepped forward with his usual swagger. "Well, the only real danger comes from the High Elf Queen's fleet. Her forces control most of the Central Continent's waters. If we run into them... we'll have to act fast."

Broken's expression tightened slightly. "Queen Yvaeris..." he murmured. "She moves easily, far too easily. I've encountered her before. So have Grill, Bloom, and Vallrick. She has a way of showing up where you least expect."
He looked around the room. "So yes, our priority is to avoid direct contact with her forces. At all costs."
Everyone nodded again, the weight of those words sinking in.
With the coordination on the ship finalized and the course locked in, Broken shifted his focus toward something equally pressing—perhaps even more personal.
A blink later, he stood once again on the earth of Vensalor Island.
The island had changed.

From what once was an untamed floating mass, it now pulsed with silent industry. Workers moved across the land with purpose. The roads, though subtle and designed to blend into the landscape—were beginning to take shape, winding between structures that sank into the terrain rather than jutting out.
Everything was built to respect the flow of nature, using underground levels, natural camouflage, and seamless architecture. From a distance, the island still looked untouched—wild and ancient.
He didn't speak to anyone.
Didn't slow.
Only Cecilia appeared, his guardian spirit, floating beside him with her usual serene glow.
"Will you continue the Tower Trial, Master?" she asked softly.
Broken kept walking.
Soon, the great spire of the Tower came into view.
He let out a breath and offered a dry smile. "Well, Floor 30's been... irritating. I didn't expect the challenge to get this annoying."
Cecilia giggled, her tone light and teasing. "Perhaps now, Master, you finally understand how your opponents have felt all this time."
Broken let out a short sigh. "Yeah... maybe I do. Still, I've learned more from this floor than the last ten combined."
Without another word, he stepped forward.
And in the next blink. He was inside.

Back within the familiar dark stone chambers of the Tower. The air was still, heavy with quiet pressure. The architecture remained unchanged—every floor eerily similar to the one before it. Yet this one carried a tension unique to Floor 30.
As the challenge initiated, the space around him shifted.
And then... a figure began to materialize ahead of him.
Step by step, they emerged from the mist, taking shape under the glow of the trial's light.
Someone was waiting.
And the figure that stood before him... was himself.
No—more precisely, it was his clone.
The Trial of Floor 20s had always been brutal, but this? This was the most relentless test yet. A perfect mirror. A reflection not just of his strength, but of his choices.
Every stat, every skill, every item he owned—this clone had access to them all.
And that was why, despite dozens of attempts, Broken still hadn't managed to win.
He'd lost count of how many times he'd stood in this chamber, only to be forced back, again and again, by himself.

The clone stepped forward with its usual detached expression—face emotionless, gaze cold and calculating. Without a word, it raised its hand and summoned the full armor. The metal gleamed under the tower's eerie light.
And then—the Abyssal Wavebreaker Spear materialized in its hand.
Broken gave a small smirk despite himself.
Of course it chose the spear.
It agreed—the spear was the most suitable weapon for a true duel.
But what made this battle so damn difficult wasn't just the gear or the power.
It was the discipline.
The clone didn't waste energy.
It didn't spam big skills.
It didn't get emotional.
It waited, calculated—and when the moment was right, it struck with terrifying precision. Martial mastery combined with Broken's own finely-honed instincts, sharpened to perfection.
It was like fighting an ideal version of himself—one that didn't tire, didn't hesitate, didn't break.
And now... it raised the spear again.
No preamble. No flourish.
Just the silent command written in its stance:
Let's go. Another battle.
Broken exhaled, tightened his grip around his own weapon, and lowered into a stance.
"Alright," he muttered. "Let's see which one of us deserves to move forward."
Thanks to this clone, his battle instincts had evolved.
This wasn't just a trial anymore.
It had become something far more valuable.

chapters.title: Chapter 899: He Fights Like Me
paragraphs: The battle always opened with a test of strength—an exchange of spear attacks. Both Broken and his clone charged around the wide arena, circling each other in relentless motion. Then came the resounding clash of metal against metal, sharp and unforgiving. It was a grueling beginning, one that immediately began to sap Broken's time and stamina.
What made it worse, what gnawed at the edge of his focus—was the realization that this clone was good. Too good. Ridiculously skilled with the spear.

And for some strange reason, Broken couldn't shake the feeling that this clone wasn't just a copy. Not exactly. There was something off, something different in the way he fought. Because, if he was honest, he didn't handle a spear like that.

Not with that precision, not with that sheer, fluid mastery. It was like fighting a version of himself that had somehow perfected a part of his own skillset far beyond his current level. It was a little bit hilarious. And a whole lot frustrating.
They exchanged blows—lunging, retreating, crashing their weapons together with brutal efficiency. Again and again. Strike, dodge, thrust, parry. And despite everything, Broken was holding his own.

He had come a long way, after all. The battles and trials he'd survived on the previous floors had shaped him, molded him into a far better fighter than he used to be. His reflexes were sharper, his movements cleaner. He was growing, adapting—right here in the thick of it.

But no matter how far he'd come, the clone still had the upper hand in one infuriating area: his ability to seamlessly shift his gear mid-combat. The way he could swap out armor and weapons in the blink of an eye—always at the perfect moment—was a nightmare to deal with.
It wasn't just a trick. It was a strategy. A deadly one.

Like the moment Broken left the smallest opening—a slight misstep in his footwork—and the clone was already darting in. A blur of motion, aiming straight for the gap. There wasn't even a chance to raise a block.
[Water Domain (Conditional Active Skill) activated]

A surge of water exploded from Broken's cape. In seconds, it swelled, expanding fast and wide. The clone was just within reach, on the verge of being trapped inside the watery domain. It was the perfect chance. Broken could turn the tables.
But the clone was always one move ahead.
At the very last instant, he switched armor. The glint of molten metal replacing his previous gear. He'd equipped the Molten Bulwark. The same armor Broken had once earned in the depths of Hell.
And then it happened.

Twin wings of fire erupted from the clone's back, spreading wide with a blast of heat and power. With a powerful dive, he launched himself upward and away, dodging the edges of the Water Domain just in time. He broke free of the trap as if it had never been there.
Damn. That was a flawless combination. Bold, quick, and terrifyingly effective.

Broken had never used that armor in front of anyone. But here, there were no secrets, no limits. Both he and the clone had access to everything they'd earned—every skill, every weapon, every piece of gear.

And just as the clone broke away to a safe distance, it swiftly switched to the Golden Bow of Artemis. In one fluid motion, arrows began flying through the air—each shot disrupting Broken's movement with brutal precision.

The clone wasn't just aiming to hurt him—he was choking his momentum, keeping him on the defensive. Arrow after arrow rained down, fast and unrelenting, wearing away Broken's stamina and shattering his defenses piece by piece.
Then... in the blink of an eye, it was over.
Broken found himself outside the tower once more.

He exhaled sharply, the weight of exhaustion pressing down on him like a lead blanket. And there she was—Cecilia, still waiting patiently nearby. When she saw his weary expression, a soft laugh escaped her lips.
This had been his fifth attempt today alone. Five brutal challenges, and still, he hadn't cleared the floor as he'd hoped.
"How's the progress, Master?" she asked. "Have you figured out how to beat the clone yet?"

Broken walked slowly toward the edge of the rocky cave, where he dropped himself onto a smooth stone. The adrenaline was still buzzing in his veins, and the tension of battle clung to him like static.
"Honestly? Not yet," he admitted, his voice flat but honest. The truth was, he still had no idea how to defeat that thing.
"It could be," Cecilia said, tilting her head slightly, "that you haven't figured out how to beat the clone... or maybe, I think you're actually enjoying the fight a little too much?"
Broken gave a small laugh at that. "I can't lie—I do enjoy fighting the clone. I mean, it's the perfect training. A real duel against a powerful opponent, and I get to do it over and over again."
"Surely, you must feel some pride in your own clone, right, Master?"
He fell silent for a moment.
Because deep down, he knew she was right. There was something terrifying about facing a version of himself that had full access to all his skills, all his gear—no holds barred.

This clone didn't just copy his power. He understood how to wield it. With terrifying versatility, the clone could shift between close-quarters combat, long-range barrages, sweeping area attacks, precise single strikes, stealth tactics—whatever the situation demanded, the clone adapted effortlessly.
It was like fighting a master strategist who had spent a lifetime studying his every move.
And somehow... that made it all the more thrilling.

Should Broken hold off on finishing the challenge just for the sake of personal training? The thought crossed his mind, especially with how much he was learning from each encounter. But deep down, he knew it wasn't a luxury he could afford. Not now.

There were harder challenges waiting for him beyond this. Far worse than the clone. And the reward from completing this floor wasn't just a bonus—it was essential. He needed it. Which meant he couldn't waste time anymore. He had to finish this. Fast.

"If only I could test the clone against everyone I know," he muttered with a lopsided grin. "Like... it'd be fun to see how the clone holds up against Nerisa. At least then I'd get a sense of whether I actually stand a chance against the queen."
Cecilia raised an eyebrow, half amused. "Surely, you don't mean to stir up trouble with the queen, do you, Master?"
"No, no... she's an ally," Broken replied with a chuckle. "And I've got no plans to piss off the ruler of the sea. Not yet, at least. She's... very useful to me."
After that, he fell into a familiar rhythm—silence, study, reflection.
He spent the next stretch of time poring over the fight. He replayed the recording of his most recent battle with the clone, eyes sharp and focused.

Every motion, every swap of armor, every perfectly timed skill activation—he studied it all. He took notes, made mental diagrams, tracked patterns. It was like watching a masterclass in combat tactics, only the instructor was himself. Or at least a version of himself that had weaponized every ounce of his potential.
It was fascinating.

The clone offered more insight and inspiration than any opponent he'd faced before. There were combinations Broken had never even thought to try, tactics he'd never dared experiment with. Seeing them in action—against himself, no less—opened a dozen new doors.
And now, he was determined to walk through them.
Because this wasn't just training anymore.
It was evolution.
And so it went—again and again. Broken kept challenging the floor, stepping into the arena only to be thrown back out. Failure. Then failure again. And again.
Or perhaps, more accurately... he was gaining experience. More experience.

After more than two hundred battles—spread over a stretch of relentless effort—Broken finally reached a point where he felt it. A quiet certainty deep in his bones. He had squeezed every last drop of knowledge, strategy, and instinct from this trial.
That day, he let out a long breath, heavy but calm. Enough. He had done enough.
"How many more battles are you planning to do for this floor's challenge, Master?" Cecilia asked.
Broken let a small grin pull at the corner of his mouth. "I think this will be the last one."
With that, he left the floating island behind and made his way back to the ship.
Waiting for him on the deck was a girl with wavy chestnut hair, her signature grin already stretched wide as she came bouncing up to him.
"Hi," SexyGrill chirped. "Still not giving up, huh?"

He'd tried this path before—using her buffs in the fight—and had learned something important. The clone, for all its terrifying mastery, had a limitation. It couldn't replicate external buffs—especially the divine enhancement he received from her.
It was a little disappointing, sure. But also, deeply reassuring.
Because it meant one thing: Broken could force the win. All he needed was that extra edge.
"Grill, I need the level boost," he said casually.
"Sure thing... I'll stick around till sunset, just in case you need another shot," she replied, flashing a wink.
"No need," he said, cracking his neck. "This ends now."
The moment her boost took effect, he stepped back into the tower, as the familiar, mirrored form of his clone emerged once more.
This was it.
If he lost now, even with the level boost—after everything he'd endured and studied—it would be beyond humiliating.
"Now," he growled, his voice low and fierce, "give me the access gate, you fuckin' tower."

The moment her boost took effect, he stepped back into the tower, as the familiar, mirrored form of his clone emerged once more.
This was it.
If he lost now, even with the level boost—after everything he'd endured and studied—it would be beyond humiliating.
"Now," he growled, his voice low and fierce, "give me the access gate, you fuckin' tower."

chapters.title: Chapter 900: What Lies Beyond the North
paragraphs: Broken's spear swept cleanly through the clone's neck in a final, decisive strike.
Yes.
At last, the clone's health dropped to zero—and the moment it did, a glowing notification appeared in front of Broken, as clear and final as a victory bell.
This time, it wasn't just a win. It was a perfect score.
He exhaled, the breath long and shaky as the adrenaline drained from his body. Then, right before him, a shimmering token emerged from the air. He reached out and took it gently into his hand.
This was it. The item he had fought tooth and nail to earn.
The gate.
He turned and exited the tower, stepping back into the open world where the cool air hit his face and the weight of exhaustion began to settle into his limbs. Floating there waiting was Cecilia.
"You finally completed the challenge, Master."
"Yeah," he said, offering a small, wry smile. "With a little help."

There was irony in his tone, and it hung there between them. Because he knew—it wasn't a true victory. Not yet. He hadn't beaten the clone in pure, even combat. The boost from SexyGrill's Divine Champion blessing had tipped the scales in his favor.
It was enough to win, yes—but not enough to satisfy the deep, quiet part of him that demanded a worthy fight.
Still, the challenge could be revisited later. He could always return, stronger, sharper, and take down the clone on equal footing. But for now, he had what he needed.
The gate.
And the next step was to see if it actually worked.
"You're certain this can be used properly, Cecilia?" he asked.
"Yes, Master. You can test it immediately if you like," she replied with calm certainty.
Of course he would.
Without wasting another second, Broken made his way back to the golem ship. He stepped aboard, moving through its familiar corridors until he began scouting for the perfect spot to plant the gate.
At first, the obvious choice seemed to be his private chamber. But then he paused. Considered. Things had changed.

Now that the gate could serve as a passage from Vensalor Island, there was a new possibility. He could bring others aboard the ship. And if that was going to happen... privacy wasn't the priority. Accessibility was.
He made his decision.
Instead of his room, he would plant the gate in the main hall—a wide, central space where people naturally gathered. It was a communal area, one that made far more sense for future arrivals.
Broken set up the gate without ceremony, as curious crew members of the ship began to gather around him.
And then—there it was.
In a blink, the gate materialized before them, taking the form of a large wooden door. And just as quickly as it appeared, it vanished again into thin air.
"Don't you think you should test it?" SexyGrill asked, standing just to his side, her arms crossed casually.
"Why would we need to?" Ronan chimed in before Broken could reply. "Look at it—it's still anchored even while the ship's moving. That alone proves it's stable."
"Huh. That actually makes sense," SexyGrill said, nodding thoughtfully.
"So... this means you could just bring Queen Nerisa here whenever you feel like it, right, Broken?" This time the remark came from Vallrick.
SexyGrill was the first to react. "You always have the worst ideas, don't you?" she said, narrowing her eyes. "We've got enough peace on this ship without her shaking things up, you know?"

Ronan chuckled, clearly amused. "Come on, the Queen fought an entire battalion from Valantar City by herself? That was insane. The power we usually only see ruling the seas? Turns out it's even more terrifying on land."

Broken glanced over his shoulder at them, the corner of his mouth twitching in amusement. "No... actually, this makes it easier for me to visit Queen Nerisa. I can just as easily return here afterward—or head straight to Slumdon, or even the capital of the Dissidia Kingdom. The gate makes that all effortless."
"That's a perfect tool for you, King," Mizuki chimed in, giggling softly. Her voice was sweet, but her grin hinted at mischief. Everyone turned toward her.
"Yes, I mean... King Broken can now visit any of his wives' rooms whenever he likes." She continued, teasingly.
A heavy silence followed.
"That is an incredibly lame idea," SexyGrill muttered. "But knowing Broken? He'll probably do it anyway."

Broken sighed, rubbing the back of his neck. "Keep that imagination to yourself, Mizuki. I'm heading out now. Let me know if anything urgent comes up. And please, don't make it urgent unless it really is."
And with that, his form shimmered—and he logged out of the game.

Leon stepped out of his capsule device and let his gaze sweep across the room. In the center was a cozy lounging area—a set of sofas arranged in a semi-circle around a massive screen that dominated the wall. He squinted slightly when he noticed someone sitting there.
It was late afternoon, judging by the light slanting in through the high windows, and to his surprise, Freya was already here.

That was unusual. Normally, she gave him a heads-up before visiting. At the very least, she'd shoot him a message. But this... this felt like old times. Back when she used to drop by whenever she felt like it, claiming the space as casually as if it were her own.
He didn't say anything. Just walked over and sank into the seat beside her, while she munched on chips and kept her eyes fixed on whatever random news was playing on the enormous screen.
They stayed like that for a while. No words, just sitting in shared silence, watching the steady stream of headlines and images flicker past.
Then, finally, she broke it.
"Why do you look so bored?" she asked, her voice playful. "Running low on real challenges? I have a feeling everything you've faced lately has been way too easy." She giggled lightly.
"Don't jinx me," Leon muttered, giving her a sideways glance. "You do remember where I'm heading next, right?
Freya let out another giggle, clearly unbothered. "Oh, I know. But trust me, something big is coming. Very big. And I think it'll be just the thing to wipe that bored expression off your face."
Leon raised an eyebrow, skeptical. "I'm always suspicious when you say things like that. I don't trust your dramatic foreshadowing."
In response, Freya nudged him in the side with her elbow, grinning. Right then, the channel on the screen changed—and this time, Leon's attention locked onto it immediately.
On the screen, a female presenter appeared, standing in what looked like an urban setting—though something about it felt entirely alien to Broken.

Massive stone structures loomed behind her, towering and strangely shaped. They didn't resemble any ordinary buildings; the scale alone was off, especially when compared to the human-sized figure of the presenter standing in front of them.

"Since the announcement of the royal quest by the High Elf Queen," she said, "this unprecedented hunt has drawn the attention of countless adventurers. What began as a regional effort has now expanded into an international pursuit, with several of the largest guilds mobilizing their top members. The search continues to intensify, and all eyes have turned toward a single destination..."
She paused for emphasis, the camera panning slightly to reveal the full scale of the monumental buildings behind her.
"...the North Continent."
Leon's head tilted slightly as his brows furrowed. "Wait... North Continent?"

Freya nodded, her gaze still fixed on the screen. "Yes... it seems the High Elf Queen's not playing around with this one. She's mobilizing everything—including the power of the players—to push her mission forward."
"So, the Queen really believes Ivana is in the North Continent?"

"It's starting to look that way. And apparently, Maylock wasn't the only one to come to that conclusion. Now that she's teamed up with players from across the world, the hunt's escalated—and more people are getting involved by the day."
"Yes, this is directly tied to the long-standing legends of Yunatea," the presenter continued, her expression turning serious.

"Specifically, the ancient conflict involving the Ancestral Divine Champions. Ever since the return of the Dragon Princess—an event that unfolded during the war in the Dissidia Kingdom—the High Elf Queen has intensified her pursuit of their primary enemy.

"Sources suggest that the target may very well be located here, on the North Continent. And although this continent has long held a reputation as the least favored destination for adventurers, that hasn't stopped the flood of interest. More and more are arriving every day.
"From our location, we'll be covering the movements of several major guilds that have already made their presence known. We'll follow this unfolding hunt as it happens—right to the end.
"Will this spark another great war?
"What do you think?
"Does the Dragon Princess have the strength to face what's coming if it does?
"And if the rumors are true... Why is she here, of all places?"
"Could this have something to do with the Giant race that ruled this land?"
